images.caption: General Orders No. 313, War Department, Adjutant General's Office, Washington September 17, 1863.  "The fort at Rosier's Bluff, on the east side of the Potomac River, two miles below Alexandria, will be called Fort Foote, after Rear Admiral A. H. Foote, U.S. Navy, who died of disease June 26, 1863, and whose distinguished services in command of the United States naval forces upon the western rivers are well known. By order of the Secretary of War.

images.caption: Union Station, located at 110 Callahan Drive in the Old Town neighborhood of Alexandria, Virginia, is served by Amtrak and Virginia Railway Express. The station house was built in 1905 in the Federal Revival style, and was renovated in 1982, with additional improvements made in the mid-1990s.  The Alexandria War Dead Memoria is located outside the station, and the King Street–Old Town station of the Washington Metro lies across the tracks. Union Station was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2013.
images.alt: Union Station, located at 110 Callahan Drive in the Old Town neighborhood of Alexandria, Virginia, is served by Amtrak and Virginia Railway Express.
